Theme

Latin word

ferō

ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum

verb, irregular · Conjugation on Wiktionary

carry, bear; bring; bear, yield (of land, trees, a country); propose (terms, a law, a bill); take (something) well or badly; react to; bear, put up with

In this lexicon

  • carry

    also used · classical · Liv. 2.32.10: nē manūs ad ōs cibum ferrent; Traupman 278

  • produce

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Leg. 2.67: quae autem terra frūgēs ferre … possit; Ov. Met. 1.109: frūgēs tellūs inarāta ferēbat

  • propose

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 2.73: cum lēgem agrāriam ferret; Traupman 180, 188: lēgem ferre, propose a law; pācis condiciōnēs ferre, propose terms of peace

  • reaction

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Phil. 10.15: quōmodo ferant veterānī exercitum Brūtum habēre (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 5.2.3: quōmodo Caesar ferret dē auctōritāte perscrīptā (Lewis & Short); Traupman 109: graviter ferō (+ accusative and infinitive)

  • suffer

    also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 138: quod fors feret, ferēmus aequō animō; Traupman 387
